content.comment_body: I'm using a MacBook Pro (Retina, 13-inch, Early 2015) running macOS Catalina version 10.15.7. I installed [product_name] [version_no] and have been working with it. I downloaded [product_name] [version_no], extracted it, and now have a folder named lsc_v83_macosx.zip. Inside there is a NoVM directory containing setup.sip. After clicking setup.zip, another setup is created, but when I try to open setup, it does not work. How do I install [product_name] [version_no]? Best regards, [user_name]

The current release of [product_name] [version_no] is only compatible with OS X versions up to 10.14. It can be executed on these operating systems: Windows (Windows 7, Windows 8, Windows 10), Linux (SUSE Linux 12 sp1, kernel 3.12.74, and other distributions aligned with Java 2), and Mac OS X (versions 10.7 Lion, 10.8 Mountain Lion, 10.9 Mavericks, 10.10 Yosemite, 10.11 El Capitan, 10.12 Sierra, 10.13 High Sierra, 10.14 Mojave).

Hello, The update from [product_name] [version_no] to [product_name] [version_no] on MacOS Monterey 12.3.1 (Intel-based Mac) was successful for me only after extracting the Setup.zip file with a program called 'The Unarchiver' (example version 4.3.5). Other programs like Stuffit Expander, Keka, or the default unarchiver failed—the resulting Setup.app did not execute. Screenshot attached. Hope this is helpful.

Hi, I spent several days trying to install [version_no] on a MacBook M1 running Ventura, without success, using both archives from the web and those from [company_name]. Thanks [user_name] for recommending The Unarchiver utility. I extracted the LSC V8_3 SP1 archive and then the Setup file in Web_Installers/InstData/MacOSX/NoVM. After these two decompressions, I launched Setup (forced it to open as it was downloaded from the internet), and the installation finally completed. The USB driver was included. Thank you everyone for your contributions!

analysis.insight_summary: Users attempting to install [product_name] [version_no] on recent MacOS versions faced compatibility problems since official support only extends to MacOS versions up to 10.14. Users tried installing on newer releases such as Monterey and Ventura. Common extraction tools did not properly prepare installation files, but one user found success using a particular unarchiving program, allowing the installation with included USB drivers.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] [version_no] to easily install and function on the latest MacOS versions without issues caused by compatibility or extraction processes.
